title: Cranial nerve examination
stem: Cubicle 23. Mr Choi, 52, woke this morning with his face drooping on the left and his left eye not closing properly. Examine his cranial nerves and explain your findings.
notes:
Checked against NICE CKS (Bell's palsy), the Sullivan et al. NEJM 2007 trial (prednisolone within 72 h), and standard cranial nerve examination.

Examine II–XII systematically: II (acuity, fields, pupils, fundi), III/IV/VI (eye movements, diplopia, nystagmus, ptosis), V (sensation in three divisions, masseter, corneal reflex), VII (raise eyebrows, close eyes tightly, show teeth, puff cheeks), VIII (whisper, Rinne and Weber), IX/X (palate, gag if needed), XI (shrug and head turn), XII (tongue).

Lower motor neurone facial palsy involves the forehead (cannot raise the eyebrow); upper motor neurone (stroke) spares the forehead because of bilateral cortical innervation. Bell's palsy is a diagnosis of exclusion: check for vesicles in the ear or palate (Ramsay Hunt), parotid mass, other cranial nerve or limb signs, hearing loss, and trauma. Treatment: prednisolone 50 mg daily for 10 days (or 60 mg 5 days then taper) within 72 hours; antivirals not routinely (consider with severe palsy / Ramsay Hunt); eye protection (lubricants, tape at night) — the key complication is corneal exposure. Refer if no improvement at 3 weeks or atypical features.

Your notes list cranial nerves as a topic without detail.

steps.label: Examine cranial nerves
steps.hint: II to XII in order; compare sides; look in the ear.

II–VI.r: 6/6 both eyes, full fields, pupils equal and reactive.
Full, no diplopia, no nystagmus, no ptosis.

II–VI.t: Facial sensation in three divisions; jaw clench

VII.r: Left eye cannot close; the eye rolls up (Bell's phenomenon).

VII.t: Show your teeth; puff your cheeks
VII.r: Left mouth droops; air escapes on the left.

VII.t: Look in the ear canal and mouth
VII.mark: Looks for vesicles (Ramsay Hunt) and parotid mass

VIII–XII.r: Normal hearing; mild hyperacusis on the left.

Limbs.t: Quick limb screen: pronator drift, power

steps.label: Explain
steps.hint: Bell's palsy; prednisolone; eye care; prognosis; return advice.

opts.t: Left lower motor neurone facial palsy with no other signs: Bell's palsy, not a stroke — the forehead is involved
opts.tz: 你呢個係左邊面神經線發炎，叫 Bell's palsy，唔係中風——因為你連額頭都郁唔到，而其他神經都正常。
opts.mark: Explains LMN versus UMN and the diagnosis

opts.t: Prednisolone 50 mg daily for 10 days, started within 72 hours
opts.tz: 我會開類固醇俾你，每日食 50 mg，食十日。三日之內開始食效果最好。

opts.t: Eye lubricant drops by day, ointment and tape at night, sunglasses; return if the eye becomes red or painful
opts.tz: 因為你隻眼合唔埋，日頭要滴眼藥水，夜晚搽眼藥膏再用膠布貼住，出街戴太陽眼鏡。如果隻眼變紅或者痛，要即刻返嚟。

opts.t: Most recover within 3–6 months; review if not improving at 3 weeks
opts.tz: 大部分人三至六個月內會好返。如果三個禮拜都冇改善，要返嚟覆診。
我淨係開抗病毒藥俾你，唔使食類固醇。
opts.r: Antivirals alone are not effective; steroids are the treatment.

qs.q: Why is the forehead spared in a stroke?
qs.a: The upper face has bilateral cortical supply
wrong: The frontalis is supplied by the trigeminal nerve instead
It is not spared in a stroke

qs.q: Ramsay Hunt syndrome is caused by…
qs.a: VZV reactivation in the geniculate ganglion

wrong: A stroke in the following month
